name: dev.htsapi/mcp
title: htsapi.dev
description: HTS with its legal notes, 222,000+ CBP rulings with status, what they quote on a heading. Keyless.

tools.name: lookup_hts_code
tools.description:
The tariff schedule, one level at a time, the way a classifier reads it. No code: the 22
    sections and their chapters, for goods no ruling covers. A chapter (82) lists its headings
    with their legal text; a heading (8205) lists its subheadings in words; a subheading or line
    gives its path from the heading (an "Other" line says what it is not), base rates with the
    special-rate programs named, the 10-digit lines under it and the newest current CBP rulings
    under it. A code no longer in the schedule falls back to the nearest level that is. What
    importers paid is a separate tool, importers_paid.

code.description: An HTS chapter, heading or code, 2 to 10 digits, dotted or not (82, 8205, 8205.51, 8205517500). Leave it out for the sections and chapters.
code.title: Code

tools.name: importers_paid
tools.description:
What importers from a country actually paid on a code in the latest 3 months Census has
    published: base rate plus Chapter 99 duties (Section 301, 232 and the like), as a percent of
    value, by month. Not the duty a shipment will owe today (Census is about 2 months behind and
    the rules change), and anti-dumping/countervailing duties are not included. For "what will
    this cost", not for classifying.

code.description: An HTS code, 6 to 10 digits, dotted or not (8205.51.30).
code.title: Code

country_of_origin.description: Country of origin: name, ISO code or common alias (China, CN, PRC, Viet Nam).
country_of_origin.title: Country Of Origin

tools.name: get_notes
tools.description:
The legal text that decides between headings, from the official US schedule. With a code:
    its section's notes and its chapter's notes, subheading notes, Additional U.S. Notes and
    statistical notes. These have legal force (GRI 1): they exclude goods from a chapter ("this
    chapter does not cover...") and define terms. Without a code: the General Rules of
    Interpretation and the Additional U.S. Rules of Interpretation. The WCO Explanatory Notes are
    not included (copyrighted); heading_scope gives the passages CBP rulings quote from them.

code.description: Any HTS chapter, heading or code (82, 8205, 8205.51.30): its section's and chapter's notes. Leave it out for the General Rules of Interpretation.
code.title: Code

tools.name: heading_scope
tools.description:
What CBP's rulings quote and decide on a heading: for deciding whether a product falls in it.
    Give the product to get what decides for it first. `passages`: the lines rulings quote when
    deciding (mostly from the WCO Explanatory Notes, not published free; fragments, not the whole
    note), each with the rulings
    that quote it: their goods, HQ or NY, date, status and what CBP concluded; `exclusion` marks
    text on what the heading does not cover. `notes_applied`: the legal notes rulings applied to
    the heading. `cited_without_quote`: rulings that relied on its explanatory note without quoting
    it. Each passage is as a ruling quotes it.

heading.description: An HTS heading (9505) or any code under it (9505.10.25).
heading.title: Heading

product.description: The product in plain words. Puts first the passages and rulings on goods closest to it: what decides for this product, not what is quoted most.
product.title: Product

tools.name: rulings_under_code
tools.description:
Every CBP ruling that classifies goods under a code: for checking a code someone already
    has. `rulings` are current (not revoked), newest first, or closest to `product` first, each
    with what its goods were; `moved_away` are rulings CBP revoked off this code and the codes the
    revoking ruling put the goods under. If similar goods were moved away, the code is in doubt.

code.description: An HTS heading, subheading or line, 4 to 10 digits (8205, 8205.51, 8205.51.30.30). Old codes no longer in the schedule work too.
code.title: Code

product.description: Optional: the product in plain words, to put the rulings closest to it first.
product.title: Product

offset.description: Rulings to skip, for the next page.
offset.title: Offset

tools.name: search_rulings
tools.description:
CBP rulings for a product described in plain words, by meaning. Each ruling comes with
    its HTS codes, its status (current, modified, superseded) and the product facts CBP
    classified. `by_code` lists the subheadings current rulings point to, in the order of the rulings,
    each with its HQ rulings, newest ruling and `lines`: the full codes under it with the rulings
    for each, which is where the facts that decide between lines show.

query.description: The product in plain words: what it is, what it is made of, what it is for.
query.title: Query

tools.name: get_ruling
tools.description:
One CBP ruling: its full text, HTS codes, status and, when revoked or modified, the ruling
    that did it, the codes it moved the goods to, and the sentence that says so. Codes the
    current schedule no longer has are listed in `obsolete_codes`. `cites`: the explanatory
    notes, legal notes and GRIs it relies on (heading_scope shows what rulings say a heading covers).

ruling_number.description: A CBP ruling number: N338413, H301540, 881984.
ruling_number.title: Ruling Number

tools.name: classify_product
tools.description:
Classify a product to a US HTS code. COSTS 1 CREDIT (refunded if it fails). Takes 10-60 s.

    Read `answer` first. `answer.code` is as deep as the facts given decide (10 digits when they
    do). When they do not, `answer.options` are the codes it could be, each with its `condition`,
    base rate and `importers_paid`, and `answer.question` is the fact that decides: ask the user,
    then call again with the answer added to the description (a new call, 1 credit).
    `candidates` carry the reasoning and the CBP rulings behind each code.

description.description: What the product is, what it is made of and what it is for, in plain words (3-2000 characters). Several listings of the same product may be pasted together.
description.title: Description

country_of_origin.description: Country of origin: name, ISO code or common alias (China, CN, PRC, Viet Nam). Adds what importers from there paid on the code (Census, the latest 3 published months).
country_of_origin.title: Country Of Origin

material.description: Main material, if not already in the description.
material.title: Material
